summary: Erwin Rousselle studied in Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, and TU Darmstadt under Krause, Walleser, and von Staël-Holstein. He held posts at Peking University (1924–1929), Goethe University Frankfurt (from 1931), Tsinghua, and Yenching, working in sinology and Buddhist studies.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Copenhagen. In 1992, he served as a visiting researcher at Otani University.

Esei Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His academic posts include assistant professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Eshin Nishimura studied at Hanazono and Kyoto universities, Pendle Hill, and under Zenkei Shibayama. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Carleton College and served as director of the IRIZ and president of Hanazono University (2002–2005).

Esho Mikogami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003. He founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū and served as president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Studies Association in 1997.

Esho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He later served as a professor at Osaka University (circa 1971–1982) and held a post at Ritsumeikan University (circa 1982–1989).
Eshun Otsuka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied as a research student at Taisho University, where he also held a research student post attested in 2013.
Eshō Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of the Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo (attested 1999) and president of the Kyushu Ryukoku Society (attested 2002).

Ester Bianchi, a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earned her PhD from Ca' Foscari and EPHE under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna. She has taught at the University of Perugia since circa 2007.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosophy scholar who studied at Ghent University from circa 1953 to 1965. He subsequently held a faculty post at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as an assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a special research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch studied at Leipzig and under Georg Bühler in Vienna. Specializing in Indology, he served as Government Epigraphist in India (1886–1903) and held the chair of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg from 1903 to 1925.

Eugen Pander was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga. In 1881, he held a post at Tongwen Guan as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German.

Eugen Prym was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1861 to 1867 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1870 to 1913.
Eugen Wilhelm was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology who studied under August Schleicher. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Obermiller specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from circa 1921 to 1925. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the USSR Academy of Sciences.

Eugene Watson Burlingame was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, Johns Hopkins University, and Yale University, where he lectured on Pāli from circa 1917 to 1932.

Eugene Y. Wang studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. Specializing in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, he held posts at the University of Chicago and became Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University.

Eugenio d'Ors was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (circa 1899–1905) and Universidad Central (circa 1905–1913). He later held an academic post at Universidad Central from circa 1927 until 1954.
Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck was a linguist who completed his studies at Leiden University between circa 1932 and 1941. He later served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983.
